title: gittr file fetch — where files come from
how: Open this JSON in NetDraw (Open button), then click Journey and walk the steps.

nodes.label: Where do files come from?
nodes.notes: Opening a repo on gittr does not mean the files live on gittr.space. The Code tab races announced clone URLs. First non-empty tree wins. This map is that race.

nodes.label: Human · Code tab
nodes.notes: Opens /npub/repo. Wants a file list and README. Does not git clone on the laptop — the gittr server fetches.

nodes.label: AI agent
nodes.notes: Does not run the Code-tab race. Calls gittr-mcp getFile or bridgeListFiles — a shorter path, not full UI parity.

nodes.label: git clone / SSH
nodes.notes: Bypasses the Code tab. Talks straight to git.gittr.space (or another clone host). Same bytes, different door.

nodes.label: Browser drafts
nodes.notes: Owned edits, uploads, and large GIFs live in the tab first. If you already rewrote a file, that body wins over the network. Clearing storage does not delete a published repo.

nodes.label: gittr Client ★
nodes.notes: git-source-fetcher.ts + RepoCodePage. Waits for kind 30617. Then races clone[] / source. Prefers GitHub/GitLab/Codeberg/self-hosted before GRASP. First non-empty tree wins. README follows that winner immediately.

nodes.label: Nostr 30617
nodes.notes: The announcement says where git lives. Published clone[] and source tags are the map. If that event has no clone URLs after the relay query finishes, well-known GRASP HTTPS URLs are filled in.

nodes.label: GitHub / GitLab / Codeberg
nodes.notes: Forge upstream. Tried first when mixed with GRASP. Fetched via GET /api/git/repo-files and /api/git/file-content on the gittr server.

nodes.label: Self-hosted / Freebox
nodes.notes: Non-GRASP hosts, including /npub/… on a home box. parseGitSource type self-hosted-git. Only GET /api/git/repo-files. The host must be reachable from gittr.space — *.local and 192.168.* are rejected.

nodes.label: gitnostr Bridge
nodes.notes: GET /api/nostr/repo/files reads repositoryDir/{pubkey}/{repo}.git. 404 is normal when clone[] is not this host. Bare trees are kept only if clone[] lists this host. SSH/HTTPS git clone hits the same disk.

nodes.label: Other GRASP
nodes.notes: Foreign GRASP HTTPS. Race: bridge files → GET /api/git/repo-files?sourceUrl= that clone → optional POST /api/nostr/repo/clone. First non-empty tree wins. gittr will not permanently mirror someone else's GRASP host onto git.gittr.space.

nodes.label: Iris Hashtree
nodes.notes: Recognized as type hashtree. Bridge cannot clone it. Code tab shows an Iris link + copyable git clone htree://… and skips the HTTPS race. Needs git-remote-htree / Iris Git.

nodes.label: gittr (this repo)
nodes.notes: Canonical implementation. FILE_FETCHING_INSIGHTS.md. npm run test:regressions in ui/. Companion repos copy docs/snippets from here.

nodes.label: gittr-mcp
nodes.notes: getFile: bridge file-content, then a few hardcoded GRASP /raw/ hosts. Not the Code-tab order (no 30617 clone[] race, no home Freebox repo-files). Prefer bridgeListFiles after importRemoteToBridge / mirrorRepo.

nodes.label: gitnostr (standalone)
nodes.notes: Public standalone of the bridge. Same Go as gittr's ui/gitnostr/. Stores the bare repos the APIs read. file-fetch-flow.md is the bridge half of this picture.

nodes.label: gittr-helper-tools
nodes.notes: Integrator copy of parseGitSource — not a live host. Teaching extract: GRASP vs self-hosted /npub/, EOSE before inferred mirrors. Keep in sync with git-source-fetcher.ts (including htree://).

steps.note: Where do Code-tab files come from? Not 'from gittr' as a blob store. gittr races the clone URLs on the Nostr announcement. First non-empty tree wins.
Three doors. A human opens the Code tab. An agent calls MCP. A laptop runs git clone. Same bytes on disk — different paths.
You are here: the gittr Client. It orchestrates the race. It does not keep a second copy of every repo — it reads announced hosts (and the local bridge when clone[] says so).
Step 1 — browser drafts. localStorage and IndexedDB win if you already edited or uploaded. Large GIFs live in IDB so they do not blow the 5 MB quota.
Step 2 — ask Nostr. Kind 30617 clone[] and source tags are the map. Well-known GRASP HTTPS is filled in after the relay query if that event has no clone URLs.

Step 3 — race those URLs. Prefer GitHub / GitLab / Codeberg / self-hosted before GRASP so a dead ngit host does not stall the tree for ~45s. The gittr server does the fetch — your NAS must be public, not 192.168.*
Same race includes the gitnostr bridge (bare repo on git.gittr.space) and other GRASP clones (ngit, shakespeare, …). First non-empty tree wins. README and click-to-open follow that winner.
htree:// is Iris Hashtree — not HTTPS git. gittr labels it and skips the race. Open Iris Git or clone with git-remote-htree. The bridge cannot fetch it.

Agents skip the Code-tab race. gittr-mcp getFile hits the bridge first, then a few hardcoded GRASP /raw/ URLs. That is a shortcut — not Freebox, not clone[] order. Prefer bridgeListFiles after you imported or mirrored.

The code lives in four repos. gittr runs the full race. gitnostr is the disk. gittr-mcp is the agent shortcut. helper-tools is the parseGitSource snippet for other clients — not a host. Click any box for the one-line job.
